long_biography.plain_text:
Investor Tomek Ulatowski established a fellowship at Berkeley's Haas School of Business because he feared tuition costs discouraged international applicants. He remembered the opportunities the school had given him as a newcomer to America. Initially intended for students educated in Poland, the fellowship later extended to students from Ukraine, reducing the financial burden of studying abroad.

His educational giving also helped establish Warsaw's POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews. With business partner Ygal Ozechov, he paid for the international competition to select its architectural design. The pair also helped initiate and fund the Poland-Israel Youth Exchange programme, bringing young people from the two countries into contact.

confidence.reason: Both beneficiary institutions directly document the gifts, purposes and participants.
